prompt: Write an email to a colleague about the weather spoiling your garden plans. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Garden plans washed out (literally)

Hi Dana,

I hope your week is going better than mine, at least weather-wise. I wanted to share a bit of gardening woe, since you're the one person I know who will appreciate it.

You may remember I'd set aside last weekend to finally get the autumn beds in order. I had the whole plan mapped out: divide the perennials on Saturday morning, plant the garlic and spring bulbs in the afternoon, and spend Sunday mulching everything before the first frost. I'd even picked up two dozen tulip bulbs and a big bag of compost, and I was feeling very pleased with myself.

Then the forecast turned. What was supposed to be a dry, mild weekend became three straight days of steady rain, with gusty wind thrown in for good measure. By Saturday morning the beds were so waterlogged that my spade sank in like I was digging through porridge. I gave it a valiant try for about twenty minutes, but all I managed to do was compact the soil and track mud through the house. I decided the plants would forgive me for waiting more than they'd forgive me for stomping all over their roots.

The worst part is the timing. The garlic really needs to go in before the ground gets too cold, and the long-range forecast shows the temperature dropping next week. If the soil stays this soggy, I may end up planting in a rush, or skipping a season altogether. The tulip bulbs are currently sitting in my garage in a paper bag, and I keep checking on them as though they might start sprouting out of spite.

I did salvage a little something from the weekend. I spent Sunday indoors sorting my seed packets and sketching a new layout for next spring, so I suppose the time wasn't a total loss. I've also moved some of the more delicate pots onto the porch to keep them out of the worst of the wind.

If the weather clears by Thursday, I'm hoping to sneak in a couple of hours after work. Fingers crossed. If you have any tips for planting in heavy, wet clay, I'd love to hear them. I seem to remember you had a similar problem a few years ago.

Also, if you have any spare time this weekend and don't mind getting a little muddy, I'd happily trade some of my extra garlic for your help.

Thanks for letting me vent, and I hope the skies are kinder to you.

Best,
[name]
